outcomeNote: Mishna statement with a tannaitic dispute.

segments.he: מַתְנִי' הָיְתָה לְמוּדָה לִהְיוֹת רוֹאָה בִּתְחִלַּת הַוְּסָתוֹת — כׇּל הַטְּהָרוֹת שֶׁעָשְׂתָה בְּתוֹךְ הַוְּסָתוֹת טְמֵאוֹת. בְּסוֹף הַוְּסָתוֹת — כׇּל הַטְּהָרוֹת שֶׁעָשְׂתָה בְּתוֹךְ הַוְּסָתוֹת טְהוֹרוֹת.
segments.en: «MISHNA:» If a woman «was accustomed to see» the flow of blood «at the beginning of the» sensation that accompanies her «fixed» cycle, even if on one occasion she happened to experience bleeding only at the end of the sensation, «all the ritually pure items that she handled within the» duration of that sensation that accompanies her «fixed» cycle «are ritually impure.» If the woman was accustomed to experience bleeding «at the end of the» sensation that accompanies her «fixed» cycle, «all the ritually pure items that she handled within the» duration of that sensation that accompanies her «fixed» cycle «are pure.»

segments.he: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: אַף יָמִים וְשָׁעוֹת וְסָתוֹת. הָיְתָה לְמוּדָה לִהְיוֹת רוֹאָה עִם הָנֵץ הַחַמָּה — אֵינָהּ אֲסוּרָה אֶלָּא עִם הָנֵץ הַחַמָּה. רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: כׇּל הַיּוֹם שֶׁלָּהּ.
segments.en: «Rabbi Yosei says: Even» specific «days and» specific «hours» determine a fixed menstrual «cycle:» If a woman «was accustomed to see» the flow of blood on a certain day of the month «at sunrise,» it is «prohibited» for «her» to engage in intercourse with her husband «only at sunrise;» but during the night before and the following day, it is permitted for her to engage in intercourse. «Rabbi Yehuda says:» Once sunrise passed and she did not menstruate, «the entire day is hers» and she may engage in intercourse, in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Yosei; but contrary to the opinion of Rabbi Yosei, intercourse the night before is prohibited.
